design: Enumerate (S,T) exhaustively -- the dimension the tie-locus LP wrongly froze to one choice -- and obtain the four extremal points by pattern iteration. delta_square<=1 is convex and needs no pattern; the competitor loss is bounded ABOVE by aux p,q with the objective subtracting (p-q), which is the safe direction; T is forced to be the argmin by p-q <= G_U(aU+)-G_U(aU-) for every other U. No tie locus at all.
honest_verdict: THE POLYHEDRAL ROUTE IS CURRENTLY WORSE THAN THE STOCHASTIC SEARCH IT WAS MEANT TO REPLACE. At m=4 the face LP reaches 0.666 while the stochastic sweep reached 0.905106 on the same space. This is not a tuning gap to be closed by more starts: the face LP converges to 2(k-1)/(m-1), which equals 2/3 at m=4 and 4/5 at m=6.
next_cheap_test: Seed each face with a KNOWN good world instead of random starts (--seed-world). Improving a known point is the one thing the ascent was reliably good at: 1.000440 -> 1.065131 in 17 s. If the face LP cannot improve the m=6 witness either, the polyhedral route should be set aside rather than tuned further.
non_claims: Nothing here bears on the (m-1) law, which is PROVED FALSE in Lean.
The reported numbers are lower bounds over visited faces, never c*.
target: c*(m) = sup 2D/delta_square on the binary cube under StrictTopC
the_recurring_attractor: 2(k-1)/(m-1) has now captured THREE independent local instruments: the original exact LP ascent, tie-point perturbation, and the face enumeration LP. The stochastic search exceeds it (0.905 > 2/3 at m=4), so the geometry has better regions that no local polyhedral method has reached. That is the finding, and it is a finding about the methods, not about c*.
what_this_means_for_the_programme: Every instrument built so far returns a LOWER bound, and they disagree with each other. c*(m) will not be settled by a better search. It needs an UPPER bound, i.e. a proof. The face LP would supply one only if the family were enumerated completely, which is 6.4e9 faces at m=6 and 2e13 at m=8.
